title: Problems born in the laboratory

blocks.what_we_do: Connect laboratory problems to the later QC checks.
blocks.why: Low DNA yield can cause many no-calls. Contamination can increase heterozygous calls. Sample swaps can create disagreement between recorded and genetic sex or duplicates with conflicting metadata. A processing batch can affect many samples together. None of these patterns alone proves its cause: retain logs and seek laboratory confirmation before changing identities. QC means quality control, a set of checks that reduce avoidable errors before statistical testing.

blocks.troubleshooting: Stop at the first error. Check the named input and the previous step. Keep the command and console logs; do not substitute files from a different dataset version. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).
blocks.quick_check:
If many samples from one plate have low call rates, what shared cause should you investigate before attributing the pattern to disease?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

A processing or batch problem; the plate pattern suggests a shared laboratory cause but does not establish it.

</details>
